content_html:
30 Jul 2026

At conferences and meetups, and in conversations online, many Ruby developers have asked me about Ruby Central and my disagreement with them. This post is my attempt to answer the questions I’ve been getting over and over, covering: 1) what is Ruby Central doing now? 2) has the dispute over Bundler and RubyGems been resolved? 3) what has Ruby Central said about the dispute? and 4) what can Ruby developers do now?

What is Ruby Central doing now?

To talk about what Ruby Central is doing now, we need to start with a bit of historical context. What was Ruby Central doing before this saga began? About 18 months ago, Ruby Central:

  • ran 2 conferences every year, RubyConf and RailsConf
  • had an Open Source Committee with 3 members (Ufuk, Gabi, Mike)
  • funded 7 part-time community OSS contributors (André, Arun, Ellen, Gift, Irene, Josef, Martin)
  • funded 3 full-time OSS developers (Colby, Samuel, David)
  • coordinated those 10 OSS contributors across 3 major OSS projects:
    • RubyGems
    • Bundler
    • RubyGems.org

Then, about 10 months ago, Ruby Central began what core team member Ellen Dash called a “hostile takeover” of the RubyGems, Bundler, and RubyGems.org open source projects, seizing control of the projects and locking out the team that had nurtured and maintained them for over a decade.

Today, 10 months after their takeover, Ruby Central has:

  • lost 2 of 2 conferences, after ending RailsConf, cancelling a significant portion of the last RubyConf, and providing no future conference locations or dates for the first time in decades
  • lost 2 of 3 major OSS projects, by transferring Bundler & RubyGems away to Matz
  • lost 9 of 10 contributors to open source work, including:
    • 6 of 7 operators of RubyGems.org (André, Samuel, Arun, Josef, Ellen, Martin)
    • 2 of 3 full-time contributors to OSS (Samuel, David)
    • 2 of 2 OSS writers (Gift, Irene)
  • lost 3 of 3 members of the Open Source Committee (Gabi, Mike, Ufuk)
  • lost 5 of 7 board members (Kinsey, Valerie, Naijeria, Ben, Ufuk)
  • lost 3 of 3 Executive Directors (Adarsh, Chelsea, Shan)
  • lost 2 of 2 major financial sponsors (Sidekiq and Shopify, although Shopify seemingly just returned after a 9 month break)

Unlike many community non-profits (including the Python Software Foundation), Ruby Central does not hold elections for their board of directors. Despite rewriting their bylaws entirely this year, new directors are still selected exclusively by existing directors, with no public process for input or feedback. The current board consists of just 2 of the 7 members who initially approved the hostile takeover, plus 3 new members chosen by the previous board (Brandon, Jey, and Ran).

Based on Ruby Central’s public announcements, they have added exactly one new program after ending both conferences and transferring away half of their open source software: a new security project, funded by a grant from Alpha-Omega. The security project’s goal is to use Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to search for security issues in gems that have already been published. In their first monthly report for June, they reported finding a total of 5 vulnerabilities, with 1 issue at medium severity, and 4 at low or unclassified severities.

Ruby Central’s current sponsorship drive, the Ruby Alliance, has found three members willing to join: Gusto, Thoughtbot, and (very recently) Shopify. What none of the sponsorship announcement posts have mentioned is that Gusto and Thoughtbot employ two of the five Ruby Central board members. David Corson-Knowles is both a board member and a Senior Staff Engineer at Gusto. Ran Craycraft is not just President of the Ruby Central board, he is also Managing Director, Americas at Thoughtbot. That means the board members who allocate the sponsorship money are also providing that sponsorship money, a conflict of interest which neither the companies nor Ruby Central have disclosed. The final sponsor is Shopify, coming back 9 months after it was reported they demanded Ruby Central start this disaster in the first place.

Has our dispute been resolved?

No, our dispute has not been resolved. Since last October, Ruby Central has been threatening to sue me. They have not withdrawn that threat as of today.

The core of our dispute is that last September, Ruby Central hijacked the Bundler and RubyGems GitHub projects from their maintainers of over ten years. When I informed Ruby Central that I own the name Bundler, they retaliated with a threat to sue me for supposed “hacking”, a position I have always disputed.

Ruby Central has stated they will only withdraw their threat if I drop my claim they infringed the name Bundler. After I also questioned if my work as a contractor had been allowed by state labor law, they additionally started demanding that I drop any claims regarding employment as well. So far, Ruby Central has consistently said they will only withdraw their lawsuit threat if I give up my infringement claim for Bundler and any possible back pay I believe they owe me.

When the lawsuit threat did not make me drop my claims, Ruby Central then chose to give away the Bundler gem and rubygems GitHub repo to Matz. After that, all of the former maintainers made a new offer to settle. Ruby Central never replied to our offer. Instead, they restated their original offer, and only to me: they would withdraw their threat to sue only if I dropped all of my claims. I did not accept, and after four months with no further progress, I wrote a public update.

In response to my post, Ruby Central did two things at once:

First, Ruby Central told me they were actively seeking outside funding to pay a settlement to me that would end our dispute. They asked me for an amount that would fully compensate me for my attorney’s fees, the amount they might owe in back pay, plus compensation for an additional six months after I was fired. With help from an expert, I calculated an amount around $450,000, and provided that number as requested.

Despite providing that number, I have never asked for that amount of money. I provided that number at Ruby Central’s request, so they could seek funding. What I have instead asked for, consistently, is an apology for the attacks on my reputation without evidence, and the far smaller amount of reimbursement for my attorneys’ fees.

Second, at the same time as they sought funding for a settlement, Ruby Central also reported me to the FBI through their lawyer, requesting that I be criminally investigated. On March 9, 2026, Ruby Central’s lawyer informed my lawyer that he had made the report, and suggested I would need to hire a criminal defense attorney. As far as I have been able to learn, Ruby Central’s lawyer was not able to provide any evidence to the FBI with his report, since Ruby Central has not been able to find evidence that I caused any harm during their three audits of the RubyGems AWS account.

Unfortunately, it is impossible to withdraw a report to the FBI. Despite Ruby Central’s later statement to me that they don’t intend to pursue the FBI report, they gave up the ability to make that decision when they filed the report — it’s up to the FBI now, not up to them.

A few weeks after saddling me with a permanent possibility of criminal prosecution by the FBI, Ruby Central ran out of money. Their post said they “want to move forward together”, but did not take any action or answer any questions regarding their past actions. Nonetheless taking that post as a promising sign, I offered Ruby Central a new option to resolve our disagreement.

I did not ask them to return Bundler. I did not ask them for fair payment under employment law. I didn’t even ask for an apology. Instead, I asked for 1) public confirmation that I did not cause any harm to RubyGems, and 2) reimbursement for the lawyer fees I have had to pay because of their threatened lawsuit. Ruby Central then ignored that post, and multiple attempts to reach out, for six weeks.

After six weeks, Ruby Central sent me a rerun of their settlement offer, with some specific restrictions: they would withdraw their lawsuit threat if I drop my claim they infringed the Bundler trademark, drop my claim they violated employment law, and agree to non-disparagement that binds me but does not bind Ruby Central, instead only specific individuals currently associated with them.

This offer did contain one new twist. Ruby Central wrote that if I accepted they would limit their cooperation with the FBI, offering to “discourage the filing of criminal charges, and if an investigation is opened or charges filed, cooperate only to the extent required by law”. There’s just one small problem with that offer: many state and federal laws make it a crime to agree to any limits on cooperation with a criminal investigation. Needless to say, I could not accept such a settlement.

Since Ruby Central can’t withdraw their FBI report (because it’s out of their hands now), and they can’t give back the repos they took (because they don’t have them anymore), and they can’t pay any kind of compensation (because they don’t have any money), I was at a bit of a loss. What could Ruby Central even do to try to resolve this situation that they had created?

In the end, I responded with a counter-offer of my own: I would drop my infringement claim against Ruby Central over their use of the name Bundler, and I would drop my claim Ruby Central violated employment law, if they would withdraw their threat to sue me and publish an apology. I asked them to apologize for publicly accusing me of harming RubyGems.org without evidence, apologize for claiming I tried to obtain user PII when I did not, and apologize for breaking the Bundler and RubyGems governance to execute their takeover. Surprising me, Ruby Central did not object to the apology I requested.

Unfortunately, Ruby Central has continued to insist on a non-disparagement agreement that binds me, but does not bind Ruby Central. I was forced to reply that I could not accept such an unbalanced agreement.

It has been 30 days since my counter-offer. While RubyConf did take up 3 of those days, Ruby Central has not replied for the full 30 days. Their lawyer promised to provide a timeframe for their response within one day, and has not done even that. A month with no response points to a different kind of resolution: an incredibly disappointing legacy for the shattered remains of a once-legendary organization.

What has Ruby Central said about this?

Even after all of the consequences described here, Ruby Central has never acknowledged that maintainers of over ten years should not have been thrown out of their own projects. Ruby Central either does not know, or is not willing to admit, that they needlessly attacked and removed the existing team when we could have given them all the help they needed to secure their systems. Ruby Central’s public posts to date carefully offer no apologies to the maintainers.

The sole public justification they have ever offered for this hostile takeover is that they did this “to improve security”. Unfortunately, Ruby Central removed all of the experts who could have ensured they executed their takeover securely. When I responsibly disclosed Ruby Central’s failure to secure their systems, which embarrassed them, they retaliated by publicly accusing me of “hacking” and privately preparing to sue me.

As of this writing, Ruby Central has conducted no less than three separate audits, seeking evidence that I caused some sort of harm. They have not found any evidence, because (beyond revealing Ruby Central’s embarrassing failure to secure the RubyGems.org service) I did not take, damage, or harm any part the RubyGems.org service.

During the multiple months where Ruby Central ignored my offers to settle, after baselessly reporting me to the FBI, they nevertheless published a “Fracture Incident Report”, which states it was written to “provide closure”. Unfortunately for that closure, the report does not explain any of the reasons Ruby Central chose a path that destroyed their sponsorships, their volunteers, their open source projects, their staff, and their board of directors.

For example, what actions did the board actually vote to approve? What did Ruby Central expect to gain? Why did Ruby Central single me out personally, while ignoring the other maintainers? Why jump straight from being embarrassed to threatening a lawsuit? What could possibly justify involving the FBI while there is no evidence of any harm? The report answers none of these questions.

Instead, Ruby Central continues former Executive Director Shan Cureton’s public policy, even beyond her departure: no one deserves to know why any of this happened, because “they don’t need to have the story, and it isn’t their story to have”. According to Ruby Central, I don’t deserve to know why this happened, none of the former maintainers deserve to know why this happened, and no one else in the Ruby community deserves to know why this happened. Including you.

What can we do about this?

There was a time when Ruby Central did more work to support the Ruby community than any other organization in the United States. In 2004, when I first started learning Ruby, I was surprised to discover that RubyConf 2005 would be in San Diego, close enough for me to attend. I rounded up my only two friends who also liked programming, and we went together.

I saw Matz give a talk proposing the -> “stabby lambda” syntax. I tried to understand call_cc in a talk given by Jim Weirich using a Nintendo 64 to demonstrate continuations via The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. I saw the Rails core team, working toward releasing Rails 1.0 in December of that year. I joined IRC on Freenode, where I made a huge number of Ruby friends I still have today, over 20 years later. I met other students who were attending from nearby UCSD, and we are also still friends to this day.

Just over a year later, I attended the first RailsConf in 2006. I met some strangers, we became friends, and one of them invited me to apply to work at his company. That became my first full-time job, set an unrealistically high standard for managers and co-workers, and made me even more friends that I still talk to regularly today.

Ruby Central’s conferences changed my life, in the best way possible. The community that grew out of the events, talks, online chats, and shared code inspired me to contribute back — to help create and ship Bundler 1.0 in 2009, to maintain Bundler for the next 15 years, to work on RubyGems and RubyGems.org for over 10 years, and to found the non-profit Ruby Together to focus on funding and maintenance for 7 years.

When Ruby Central reached out to express interest in merging with Ruby Together, and combining my open source programs with their conference programs, I was flattered. I agreed to the merger based on their spectacular track record of conferences and community-building from 2001 to 2021.

It’s incredibly sad that today, just a few years later, Ruby Central has zero upcoming conferences for the first time in their 25 year existence. It’s even more sad that this entire dispute, far from strengthening Ruby Central as they claimed to want, has instead attacked the very community governance they were supposed to be providing.

Even beyond getting thrown out of the project that I helped create, after fundraising for a decade to keep it alive, Ruby Central’s betrayal of the community hurts. It hurts to see not just me, but a whole team of maintainers driven away from the projects they have nurtured and developed for so many years. It hurts to hear that even after all of this, it was done for no real reason anyone can explain, and produced no real benefits that anyone can point at. That’s no way to rebuild trust, or to support and grow a community.

The Ruby community deserves better.

We can create open source projects governed openly by their maintainers, like gem.coop. We can build new tools that make using Ruby better for everyone, like rv or Ruby Butler. While I have no interest in creating any more Ruby non-profits, I hope one day there will be Ruby community organizations where the directors are elected by the community, perhaps like the Python Software Foundation board.

We can’t return to the past, when Ruby Central’s conferences were popular and amazing community events, and when Ruby Together supported open source projects without claiming to own them. Instead of spending our time trying to bring back the old days, let’s work together to build Ruby a brighter future.

blocks.html_en: Based on Ruby Central’s public announcements, they have added exactly one new program after ending both conferences and transferring away half of their open source software: a new security project, funded by a grant from Alpha-Omega. The security project’s goal is to use Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to search for security issues in gems that have already been published. In their first monthly report for June, they reported finding a total of 5 vulnerabilities, with 1 issue at medium severity, and 4 at low or unclassified severities.

blocks.html_en: Ruby Central’s current sponsorship drive, the Ruby Alliance, has found three members willing to join: Gusto, Thoughtbot, and (very recently) Shopify. What none of the sponsorship announcement posts have mentioned is that Gusto and Thoughtbot employ two of the five Ruby Central board members. David Corson-Knowles is both a board member and a Senior Staff Engineer at Gusto. Ran Craycraft is not just President of the Ruby Central board, he is also Managing Director, Americas at Thoughtbot. That means the board members who allocate the sponsorship money are also providing that sponsorship money, a conflict of interest which neither the companies nor Ruby Central have disclosed. The final sponsor is Shopify, coming back 9 months after it was reported they demanded Ruby Central start this disaster in the first place.

blocks.html_en: The core of our dispute is that last September, Ruby Central hijacked the Bundler and RubyGems GitHub projects from their maintainers of over ten years. When I informed Ruby Central that I own the name Bundler, they retaliated with a threat to sue me for supposed “hacking”, a position I have always disputed.

blocks.html_en: In response to my post, Ruby Central did two things at once:

sentences.en: In response to my post, Ruby Central did two things at once:
sentences.zh: 为了回应我的帖子，Ruby Central 同时做了两件事：

blocks.html_en: First, Ruby Central told me they were actively seeking outside funding to pay a settlement to me that would end our dispute. They asked me for an amount that would fully compensate me for my attorney’s fees, the amount they might owe in back pay, plus compensation for an additional six months after I was fired. With help from an expert, I calculated an amount around $450,000, and provided that number as requested.

blocks.html_en: Despite providing that number, I have never asked for that amount of money. I provided that number at Ruby Central’s request, so they could seek funding. What I have instead asked for, consistently, is an apology for the attacks on my reputation without evidence, and the far smaller amount of reimbursement for my attorneys’ fees.

blocks.html_en: Second, at the same time as they sought funding for a settlement, Ruby Central also reported me to the FBI through their lawyer, requesting that I be criminally investigated. On March 9, 2026, Ruby Central’s lawyer informed my lawyer that he had made the report, and suggested I would need to hire a criminal defense attorney. As far as I have been able to learn, Ruby Central’s lawyer was not able to provide any evidence to the FBI with his report, since Ruby Central has not been able to find evidence that I caused any harm during their three audits of the RubyGems AWS account.

blocks.html_en: Unfortunately, it is impossible to withdraw a report to the FBI. Despite Ruby Central’s later statement to me that they don’t intend to pursue the FBI report, they gave up the ability to make that decision when they filed the report — it’s up to the FBI now, not up to them.

Nonetheless taking that post as a promising sign, I offered Ruby Central a new option to resolve our disagreement.

blocks.html_en: After six weeks, Ruby Central sent me a rerun of their settlement offer, with some specific restrictions: they would withdraw their lawsuit threat if I drop my claim they infringed the Bundler trademark, drop my claim they violated employment law, and agree to non-disparagement that binds me but does not bind Ruby Central, instead only specific individuals currently associated with them.

blocks.html_en: This offer did contain one new twist. Ruby Central wrote that if I accepted they would limit their cooperation with the FBI, offering to “discourage the filing of criminal charges, and if an investigation is opened or charges filed, cooperate only to the extent required by law”. There’s just one small problem with that offer: many state and federal laws make it a crime to agree to any limits on cooperation with a criminal investigation. Needless to say, I could not accept such a settlement.

sentences.zh: Ruby Central 写道，如果我接受，他们将限制与联邦调查局的合作，并提出“不鼓励提出刑事指控，如果展开调查或提出指控，则仅在法律要求的范围内合作”。

sentences.en: There’s just one small problem with that offer: many state and federal laws make it a crime to agree to any limits on cooperation with a criminal investigation.
sentences.zh: 这一提议只有一个小问题：许多州和联邦法律将同意对与刑事调查合作的任何限制视为犯罪。

sentences.en: Needless to say, I could not accept such a settlement.
sentences.zh: 不用说，我不能接受这样的解决方案。

blocks.html_en: Since Ruby Central can’t withdraw their FBI report (because it’s out of their hands now), and they can’t give back the repos they took (because they don’t have them anymore), and they can’t pay any kind of compensation (because they don’t have any money), I was at a bit of a loss. What could Ruby Central even do to try to resolve this situation that they had created?

sentences.en: What could Ruby Central even do to try to resolve this situation that they had created?
sentences.zh: Ruby Central 可以做些什么来尝试解决他们造成的这种情况？

blocks.html_en: In the end, I responded with a counter-offer of my own: I would drop my infringement claim against Ruby Central over their use of the name Bundler, and I would drop my claim Ruby Central violated employment law, if they would withdraw their threat to sue me and publish an apology. I asked them to apologize for publicly accusing me of harming RubyGems.org without evidence, apologize for claiming I tried to obtain user PII when I did not, and apologize for breaking the Bundler and RubyGems governance to execute their takeover. Surprising me, Ruby Central did not object to the apology I requested.

sentences.en: In the end, I responded with a counter-offer of my own: I would drop my infringement claim against Ruby Central over their use of the name Bundler, and I would drop my claim Ruby Central violated employment law, if they would withdraw their threat to sue me and publish an apology.

sentences.en: Surprising me, Ruby Central did not object to the apology I requested.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，Ruby Central 并没有反对我要求的道歉。

blocks.html_en: Unfortunately, Ruby Central has continued to insist on a non-disparagement agreement that binds me, but does not bind Ruby Central. I was forced to reply that I could not accept such an unbalanced agreement.

sentences.en: Unfortunately, Ruby Central has continued to insist on a non-disparagement agreement that binds me, but does not bind Ruby Central.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，Ruby Central 继续坚持非贬低协议，该协议对我有约束力，但对 Ruby Central 没有约束力。

sentences.en: I was forced to reply that I could not accept such an unbalanced agreement.
sentences.zh: 我被迫回答说我不能接受这样一个不平衡的协议。

blocks.html_en: It has been 30 days since my counter-offer. While RubyConf did take up 3 of those days, Ruby Central has not replied for the full 30 days. Their lawyer promised to provide a timeframe for their response within one day, and has not done even that. A month with no response points to a different kind of resolution: an incredibly disappointing legacy for the shattered remains of a once-legendary organization.

sentences.en: It has been 30 days since my counter-offer.

sentences.zh: 虽然 RubyConf 确实占用了其中 3 天，但 Ruby Central 在整整 30 天里都没有回复。

sentences.en: Their lawyer promised to provide a timeframe for their response within one day, and has not done even that.
sentences.zh: 他们的律师承诺在一天内提供答复的时间表，但甚至没有这样做。

sentences.en: A month with no response points to a different kind of resolution: an incredibly disappointing legacy for the shattered remains of a once-legendary organization.
sentences.zh: 一个月没有任何回应表明了一种不同的解决方案：对于一个曾经传奇的组织的支离破碎的残骸来说，这是一个令人难以置信的令人失望的遗产。

blocks.html_en: What has Ruby Central said about this?

sentences.en: What has Ruby Central said about this?
sentences.zh: Ruby Central 对此有何评论？

blocks.html_en: Even after all of the consequences described here, Ruby Central has never acknowledged that maintainers of over ten years should not have been thrown out of their own projects. Ruby Central either does not know, or is not willing to admit, that they needlessly attacked and removed the existing team when we could have given them all the help they needed to secure their systems. Ruby Central’s public posts to date carefully offer no apologies to the maintainers.

sentences.en: Even after all of the consequences described here, Ruby Central has never acknowledged that maintainers of over ten years should not have been thrown out of their own projects.
sentences.zh: 即使发生了这里描述的所有后果，Ruby Central 也从未承认十多年的维护者不应该被赶出自己的项目。

sentences.en: Ruby Central either does not know, or is not willing to admit, that they needlessly attacked and removed the existing team when we could have given them all the help they needed to secure their systems.
sentences.zh: Ruby Central 要么不知道，要么不愿意承认，当我们本可以为他们提供保护系统所需的所有帮助时，他们不必要地攻击并解雇了现有团队。

sentences.en: Ruby Central’s public posts to date carefully offer no apologies to the maintainers.
sentences.zh: Ruby Central 迄今为止的公开帖子谨慎地没有向维护者道歉。

blocks.html_en: The sole public justification they have ever offered for this hostile takeover is that they did this “to improve security”. When I responsibly disclosed Ruby Central’s failure to secure their systems, which embarrassed them, they retaliated by publicly accusing me of “hacking” and privately preparing to sue me.

sentences.en: The sole public justification they have ever offered for this hostile takeover is that they did this “to improve security”.
sentences.zh: 他们为这次敌意收购提供的唯一公开理由是，他们这样做是“为了提高安全性”。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, Ruby Central removed all of the experts who could have ensured they executed their takeover securely.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，Ruby Central 解雇了所有可以确保他们安全执行接管的专家。

sentences.en: When I responsibly disclosed Ruby Central’s failure to secure their systems, which embarrassed them, they retaliated by publicly accusing me of “hacking” and privately preparing to sue me.
sentences.zh: 当我负责任地披露 Ruby Central 未能保护他们的系统并让他们感到尴尬时，他们公开指责我“黑客攻击”并私下准备起诉我进行报复。

blocks.html_en: As of this writing, Ruby Central has conducted no less than three separate audits, seeking evidence that I caused some sort of harm. They have not found any evidence, because (beyond revealing Ruby Central’s embarrassing failure to secure the RubyGems.org service) I did not take, damage, or harm any part the RubyGems.org service.

sentences.en: As of this writing, Ruby Central has conducted no less than three separate audits, seeking evidence that I caused some sort of harm.
sentences.zh: 截至撰写本文时，Ruby Central 已进行了至少三项单独的审计，寻找我造成某种伤害的证据。

sentences.en: They have not found any evidence, because (beyond revealing Ruby Central’s embarrassing failure to secure the RubyGems.org service) I did not take, damage, or harm any part the RubyGems.org service.
sentences.zh: 他们没有找到任何证据，因为（除了揭露 Ruby Central 在保护 RubyGems.org 服务方面的令人尴尬的失败之外）我没有拿走、损坏或伤害 RubyGems.org 服务的任何部分。

blocks.html_en: During the multiple months where Ruby Central ignored my offers to settle, after baselessly reporting me to the FBI, they nevertheless published a “Fracture Incident Report”, which states it was written to “provide closure”. Unfortunately for that closure, the report does not explain any of the reasons Ruby Central chose a path that destroyed their sponsorships, their volunteers, their open source projects, their staff, and their board of directors.

blocks.html_en: For example, what actions did the board actually vote to approve? What did Ruby Central expect to gain? sentences.zh: 为什么 Ruby Central 单独挑衅我，而忽略其他维护者？

sentences.zh: 为什么从尴尬直接跳到威胁提起诉讼？

sentences.zh: 在没有任何损害的证据的情况下，什么可能有理由让联邦调查局介入？

blocks.html_en: Instead, Ruby Central continues former Executive Director Shan Cureton’s public policy, even beyond her departure: no one deserves to know why any of this happened, because “they don’t need to have the story, and it isn’t their story to have”. sentences.en: What can we do about this?

blocks.html_en: There was a time when Ruby Central did more work to support the Ruby community than any other organization in the United States. In 2004, when I first started learning Ruby, I was surprised to discover that RubyConf 2005 would be in San Diego, close enough for me to attend. I rounded up my only two friends who also liked programming, and we went together.

sentences.zh: 2004 年，当我第一次开始学习 Ruby 时，我惊讶地发现 RubyConf 2005 将在圣地亚哥举行，距离我很近，可以参加。

blocks.html_en: Ruby Central’s conferences changed my life, in the best way possible. The community that grew out of the events, talks, online chats, and shared code inspired me to contribute back — to help create and ship Bundler 1.0 in 2009, to maintain Bundler for the next 15 years, to work on RubyGems and RubyGems.org for over 10 years, and to found the non-profit Ruby Together to focus on funding and maintenance for 7 years.

blocks.html_en: It’s incredibly sad that today, just a few years later, Ruby Central has zero upcoming conferences for the first time in their 25 year existence. 在会议和聚会以及在线对话中，许多 Ruby 开发人员向我询问有关 Ruby Central 的问题以及我与他们的分歧。 这篇文章是我试图回答我反复提出的问题，包括：1）Ruby Central 现在在做什么？ 2）Bundler和RubyGems的争议解决了吗？ 3) Ruby Central 对于此次纠纷有何评论？ 4) Ruby 开发人员现在可以做什么？

Ruby Central 现在在做什么？

要谈论 Ruby Central 现在在做什么，我们需要从一些历史背景开始。 在这个传奇开始之前，Ruby Central 在做什么？ 大约 18 个月前，Ruby Central：

  • 每年举办 2 场会议，RubyConf 和 RailsConf
  • 有一个由 3 名成员组成的开源委员会（Ufuk、Gabi、Mike）
  • 资助 7 名兼职社区 OSS 贡献者（André、Arun、Ellen、Gift、Irene、Josef、Martin）
  • 资助 3 名全职 OSS 开发人员（Colby、Samuel、David）
  • 协调 3 个主要 OSS 项目中的 10 个 OSS 贡献者：RubyGemsBundlerRubyGems.org

然后，大约 10 个月前，Ruby Central 开始对 RubyGems、Bundler 和 RubyGems.org 开源项目进行核心团队成员 Ellen Dash 所说的“敌意收购”，夺取了这些项目的控制权，并锁定了十多年来培育和维护这些项目的团队。

今天，在他们接管 10 个月后，Ruby Central 已经：

  • 在 RailsConf 结束后，失去了 2 场会议中的 2 场，取消了上一次 RubyConf 的很大一部分，并且数十年来首次没有提供未来的会议地点或日期
  • 通过将 Bundler 和 RubyGems 转移到 Matz，失去了 3 个主要 OSS 项目中的 2 个
  • 开源工作的 10 名贡献者中失去了 9 名，其中包括： RubyGems.org 7 名操作员中的 6 名（André、Samuel、Arun、Josef、Ellen、Martin）3 名 OSS 全职贡献者中的 2 名（Samuel、David）2 名 OSS 编写者中的 2 名（Gift、Irene）
  • 失去了开源委员会 3 名成员中的 3 名（Gabi、Mike、Ufuk）
  • 董事会 7 名成员中的 5 名流失（Kinsey、Valerie、Naijeria、Ben、Ufuk）
  • 失去 3 位执行董事中的 3 位（Adarsh、Chelsea、Shan）
  • 失去了 2 个主要财务赞助商中的 2 个（Sidekiq 和 Shopify，尽管 Shopify 似乎在中断 9 个月后刚刚回归）

与许多社区非营利组织（包括 Python 软件基金会）不同，Ruby Central 不举行董事会选举。 尽管今年完全重写了章程，但新董事仍然由现有董事专门挑选，没有公开的意见或反馈程序。 目前的董事会仅由最初批准敌意收购的 7 名成员中的 2 名以及前任董事会选出的 3 名新成员（Brandon、Jey 和 Ran）组成。

根据 Ruby Central 的公开声明，在结束两次会议并转让一半的开源软件后，他们又添加了一个新项目：一个新的安全项目，由 Alpha-Omega 资助。 该安全项目的目标是使用 Anthropic 的 Project Glasswing 来搜索已发布的 gem 中的安全问题。 在 6 月份的第一份月度报告中，他们报告总共发现 5 个漏洞，其中 1 个为中等严重性问题，4 个为低度或未分类严重性问题。

Ruby Central 目前的赞助活动 Ruby Alliance 已经找到了三个愿意加入的成员：Gusto、Thoughtbot 和（最近）Shopify。 赞助公告帖子中都没有提到 Gusto 和 Thoughtbot 聘用了 Ruby Central 董事会五名成员中的两名。 David Corson-Knowles 是 Gusto 的董事会成员和高级工程师。 Ran Craycraft 不仅是 Ruby Central 董事会主席，还是 Thoughtbot 美洲区董事总经理。 这意味着分配赞助资金的董事会成员也在提供赞助资金，这是公司和 Ruby Central 都没有披露的利益冲突。 最后的赞助商是 Shopify，在有报道称他们要求 Ruby Central 首先引发这场灾难后 9 个月，Shopify 又回来了。

我们的纠纷解决了吗？

不，我们的纠纷还没有解决。 自去年十月以来，Ruby Central 一直威胁要起诉我。 截至今天，他们还没有撤回这一威胁。

我们争论的核心是，去年 9 月，Ruby Central 从其十多年的维护者手中劫持了 Bundler 和 RubyGems GitHub 项目。 当我告诉 Ruby Central 我拥有 Bundler 这个名字时，他们进行了报复，威胁要起诉我所谓的“黑客行为”，而我一直对这一立场提出异议。

Ruby Central 表示，只有当我放弃他们侵犯 Bundler 名称的指控时，他们才会撤回威胁。 在我还质疑州劳动法是否允许我作为承包商的工作后，他们也开始要求我放弃任何有关就业的索赔。 到目前为止，Ruby Central 一直表示，只有我放弃对 Bundler 的侵权索赔以及我认为他们欠我的任何可能的欠款，他们才会撤回诉讼威胁。

当诉讼威胁没有让我放弃索赔时，Ruby Central 选择将 Bundler gem 和 ruby​​gems GitHub 存储库赠送给 Matz。 之后，所有前维护者都提出了新的和解方案。 Ruby Central 从未回复我们的报价。 相反，他们重申了最初的提议，而且只对我提出：只有我放弃所有索赔，他们才会撤回起诉的威胁。 我没有接受，四个月后没有进一步进展，我写了一个公开更新。

为了回应我的帖子，Ruby Central 同时做了两件事：

首先，Ruby Central 告诉我，他们正在积极寻求外部资金，以便向我支付和解金，以结束我们的纠纷。 他们要求我提供一笔足以补偿我的律师费、他们可能拖欠的工资的金额，以及我被解雇后额外六个月的补偿金。 在专家的帮助下，我计算出金额约为 450,000 美元，并按要求提供了该数字。

尽管提供了这个号码，但我从未要求过那么多钱。 我应 Ruby Central 的要求提供了这个号码，以便他们能够寻求资金。 相反，我一贯要求的是对在没有证据的情况下对我声誉的攻击道歉，并报销我的律师费的金额要小得多。

其次，在寻求和解资金的同时，Ruby Central还通过他们的律师向FBI举报了我，要求对我进行刑事调查。 2026年3月9日，Ruby Central的律师通知我的律师，他已经做了报告，并建议我需要聘请一名刑事辩护律师。 据我所知，Ruby Central 的律师无法通过他的报告向 FBI 提供任何证据，因为 Ruby Central 无法找到证据证明我在 RubyGems AWS 账户的三次审计中造成了任何伤害。

不幸的是，不可能撤回向联邦调查局提交的报告。 尽管 Ruby Central 后来向我声明他们不打算追究 FBI 的报告，但他们在提交报告时就放弃了做出决定的能力——现在取决于 FBI，而不是他们。

在我面临联邦调查局永久刑事起诉的可能性后几周，Ruby Central 的钱就花光了。 他们的帖子称他们“希望共同前进”，但没有采取任何行动，也没有回答有关他们过去行为的任何问题。 尽管如此，我还是将这篇文章视为一个有希望的信号，为 Ruby Central 提供了一个新的选择来解决我们的分歧。

我没有要求他们归还 Bundler。 我没有要求他们根据雇佣法支付公平的报酬。 我什至没有要求道歉。 相反，我要求 1) 公开确认我没有对 RubyGems 造成任何伤害，2) 报销我因他们威胁提起诉讼而必须支付的律师费。 随后，Ruby Central 在六周内忽略了该帖子，并多次尝试联系。

六周后，Ruby Central 向我重新发出了他们的和解方案，其中包含一些具体限制：如果我放弃对他们侵犯 Bundler 商标的指控、放弃对他们违反就业法的指控，并同意不贬低（约束我但不约束 Ruby Central，而只约束当前与他们相关的特定个人），他们将撤回诉讼威胁。

这一提议确实包含了一个新的变化。 Ruby Central 写道，如果我接受，他们将限制与联邦调查局的合作，并提出“不鼓励提出刑事指控，如果展开调查或提出指控，则仅在法律要求的范围内合作”。 这一提议只有一个小问题：许多州和联邦法律将同意对与刑事调查合作的任何限制视为犯罪。 不用说，我不能接受这样的解决方案。

由于 Ruby Central 无法撤回他们的 FBI 报告（因为现在已经不在他们手中），他们无法归还他们拿走的回购协议（因为他们不再拥有它们），而且他们无法支付任何形式的补偿（因为他们没有钱），所以我有点不知所措。 Ruby Central 可以做些什么来尝试解决他们造成的这种情况？

最后，我以自己的还价进行回应：如果 Ruby Central 撤销起诉我的威胁并发表道歉声明，我将放弃对 Ruby Central 使用 Bundler 名称的侵权指控，并且放弃对 Ruby Central 违反就业法的指控。 我要求他们为在没有证据的情况下公开指责我损害 RubyGems.org 道歉，为声称我试图获取用户 PII 而实际上没有获取用户 PII 道歉，并为破坏 Bundler 和 RubyGems 治理以执行他们的接管而道歉。 令我惊讶的是，Ruby Central 并没有反对我要求的道歉。

不幸的是，Ruby Central 继续坚持非贬低协议，该协议对我有约束力，但对 Ruby Central 没有约束力。 我被迫回答说我不能接受这样一个不平衡的协议。

距离我还盘已经过去30天了。 虽然 RubyConf 确实占用了其中 3 天，但 Ruby Central 在整整 30 天里都没有回复。 他们的律师承诺在一天内提供答复的时间表，但甚至没有这样做。 一个月没有任何回应表明了一种不同的解决方案：对于一个曾经传奇的组织的支离破碎的残骸来说，这是一个令人难以置信的令人失望的遗产。

Ruby Central 对此有何评论？

即使发生了这里描述的所有后果，Ruby Central 也从未承认十多年的维护者不应该被赶出自己的项目。 Ruby Central 要么不知道，要么不愿意承认，当我们本可以为他们提供保护系统所需的所有帮助时，他们不必要地攻击并解雇了现有团队。 Ruby Central 迄今为止的公开帖子谨慎地没有向维护者道歉。

他们为这次敌意收购提供的唯一公开理由是，他们这样做是“为了提高安全性”。 不幸的是，Ruby Central 解雇了所有可以确保他们安全执行接管的专家。 当我负责任地披露 Ruby Central 未能保护他们的系统并让他们感到尴尬时，他们公开指责我“黑客攻击”并私下准备起诉我进行报复。

截至撰写本文时，Ruby Central 已进行了至少三项单独的审计，寻找我造成某种伤害的证据。 他们没有找到任何证据，因为（除了揭露 Ruby Central 在保护 RubyGems.org 服务方面的令人尴尬的失败之外）我没有拿走、损坏或伤害 RubyGems.org 服务的任何部分。

在 Ruby Central 忽视我的和解提议的几个月里，在毫无根据地向联邦调查局报告我之后，他们仍然发布了一份“骨折事件报告”，其中指出它是为了“提供结案”而编写的。 不幸的是，对于这次关闭，该报告没有解释 Ruby Central 选择一条破坏其赞助、志愿者、开源项目、员工和董事会的道路的任何原因。

例如，董事会实际投票批准了哪些行动？ Ruby Central 期望获得什么？ 为什么 Ruby Central 单独挑衅我，而忽略其他维护者？ 为什么从尴尬直接跳到威胁提起诉讼？ 在没有任何损害的证据的情况下，什么可能有理由让联邦调查局介入？ 该报告没有回答这些问题。

相反，Ruby Central 延续了前执行董事 Shan Cureton 的公共政策，甚至在她离职后也是如此：没有人应该知道为什么会发生这一切，因为“他们不需要故事，而且这也不是他们应该有的故事”。 根据 Ruby Central 的说法，我不应该知道为什么会发生这种情况，没有一个前维护者应该知道为什么会发生这种情况，Ruby 社区中的其他人也不应该知道为什么会发生这种情况。 包括你。

对此我们能做些什么呢？

曾经有一段时间，Ruby Central 为支持 Ruby 社区所做的工作比美国任何其他组织都多。 2004 年，当我第一次开始学习 Ruby 时，我惊讶地发现 RubyConf 2005 将在圣地亚哥举行，距离我很近，可以参加。 我召集了仅有的两个也喜欢编程的朋友，我们一起去了。

我看到 Matz 在演讲中提出了 -> “stabby lambda” 语法。 我试图在 Jim Weirich 的一次演讲中使用 Nintendo 64 演示《塞尔达传说：时之笛》的延续来理解 call_cc。 我看到 Rails 核心团队正致力于在当年 12 月发布 Rails 1.0。 我加入了 Freenode 上的 IRC，在那里我结识了很多 Ruby 朋友，20 多年后我仍然拥有这些朋友。 我遇到了来自附近加州大学圣地亚哥分校的其他学生，直到今天我们仍然是朋友。

一年多后，我参加了 2006 年第一届 RailsConf。 我遇到了一些陌生人，我们成为了朋友，其中一位邀请我申请到他的公司工作。 那成为我的第一份全职工作，为经理和同事设定了不切实际的高标准，并让我结识了更多的朋友，直到今天我仍然经常与之交谈。

Ruby Central 的会议以最好的方式改变了我的生活。 从这些活动、演讲、在线聊天和共享代码中成长起来的社区激励我做出回馈——在 2009 年帮助创建和发布 Bundler 1.0，在接下来的 15 年中维护 Bundler，在 RubyGems 和 RubyGems.org 上工作超过 10 年，并创建非营利性 Ruby Together 并在 7 年内专注于资助和维护。

当 Ruby Central 表示有兴趣与 Ruby Together 合并，并将我的开源程序与他们的会议程序结合起来时，我感到受宠若惊。 我同意合并是基于他们从 2001 年到 2021 年在会议和社区建设方面取得的辉煌业绩。

令人难以置信的是，仅仅几年后的今天，Ruby Central 即将举行的会议数量为零，这是 Ruby Central 成立 25 年来首次。 更可悲的是，整个争议远没有像他们声称的那样加强 Ruby Central，而是攻击了他们本应提供的社区治理。

除了被我帮助创建的项目抛弃之外，在筹集了十年资金以维持该项目的生存之后，Ruby Central 对社区的背叛也令人心痛。 不仅是我，而且整个维护团队都被赶走了他们多年来培育和开发的项目，这让我很伤心。 令人心痛的是，即使在这一切之后，这样做却没有任何人可以解释的真正原因，也没有产生任何人都可以指出的真正好处。 这无法重建信任，也无法支持和发展社区。

Ruby 社区值得更好。

我们可以创建由维护者公开管理的开源项目，例如 gem.coop。 我们可以构建新工具，让每个人都能更好地使用 Ruby，例如 rv 或 Ruby Butler。 虽然我没有兴趣创建更多的 Ruby 非营利组织，但我希望有一天会出现 Ruby 社区组织，其中的董事由社区选举产生，也许就像 Python 软件基金会董事会一样。

我们无法回到过去，那时 Ruby Central 的会议是流行且令人惊叹的社区活动，当时 Ruby Together 支持开源项目而不声称拥有它们。 让我们共同努力，打造 Ruby 更光明的未来，而不是花时间试图重温过去的时光。
